chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskhan, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the time of Dhuhr prayer, so he said: 'One cubit from the sun's declination, and the time of Asr prayer is one cubit from the time of Dhuhr, so that is four spans from the sun's declination.'

And Zurarah said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me when I asked him about that: 'Indeed, the wall of the Messenger of God's mosque was one cubit high, so when one cubit of its shadow had passed, he would pray Dhuhr, and when two cubits of its shadow had passed, he would pray Asr.'

Then he said: 'Do you know why one cubit and two cubits were established?' I said: 'Why was that established?' He said: 'For the sake of the supererogatory prayer, for you may perform supererogatory prayer from the sun's declination until the shadow passes one cubit. When your shadow reaches one cubit from the declination, you begin with the obligatory prayer and leave the supererogatory one.'

Ibn Muskhan said: He narrated to me about the one cubit and the two cubits from - Sulayman ibn Khalid, Abu Basir al-Muradi, and Husayn, the owner of al-Qalanis, and Ibn Abi Ya'fur, and those whom I cannot enumerate from them.
And in this report is explicit confirmation of what we established in the chapter: that these times were established only for the sake of the supererogatory prayer.
ai.seo_question: How is the time for Dhuhr and Asr prayers determined by shadow length in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) defines the temporal boundaries for Dhuhr and Asr prayers using shadow measurements, specifically linking the start of Asr to the shadow reaching two cubits. It clarifies that the one-cubit interval serves as a designated window for supererogatory (Nafilah) prayers, which must cease once the obligatory Dhuhr time begins. This narration is cited in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* to substantiate the scholarly consensus that these specific shadow lengths are practical markers derived from the Prophet’s practice.
